Fees

On base taker fees, Binance is cheaper (Binance 0.04% vs KuCoin 0.06%). Both reward makers (resting limit orders) with lower fees and cut rates further as your 30-day volume grows. For most active traders the fee gap is small next to the cost of a single bad liquidation — which is why position sizing matters more than chasing the lowest fee. See maker vs taker fees.

Leverage & liquidation

Binance offers the higher cap (Binance up to 125×, KuCoin up to 100×), but the headline number is a trap: at 125× a roughly 1% move liquidates you. The maintenance margin rate (≈0.4% vs ≈0.5%) also nudges your liquidation price. Check yours before entering with the liquidation calculator, or the per-exchange pages: Binance · KuCoin.

Which should you pick?

If you want the largest volume and the widest range of futures pairs, go with Binance. If a huge altcoin futures selection matters more, KuCoin fits better. Many traders keep accounts on both and route each trade to wherever the liquidity and funding are best on the day. There's no wrong answer — there is only an unplanned trade.
